hints.title: Contiguous Land Traversal Obstacle
hints.text: Counting contiguous land requires traversing every cell in an island without recounting previously visited parts. If you explore from a land cell, how can you ensure each connected land component is tallied only once?

hints.title: Component Sinking Invariant
hints.text: Each unvisited land cell marks the discovery of a distinct island. Sinking or marking all reachable neighbors ensures each component is visited exactly once.

hints.title: Iterative Grid Traversal Procedure
hints.text: Iterate through each cell of the grid. Whenever a cell contains land '1', increment the island count and initiate an expansion to all four adjacent neighbors, resetting visited land cells to '0'. Return the total count.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: M: number of grid rows (1 <= M <= 300)
N: number of grid columns (1 <= N <= 300)
complexity.notes: Every cell is visited a constant number of times. Auxiliary space is bounded by the frontier size or recursion depth.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Re-evaluating or not tracking visited cells leads to infinite loops or recounting the same island multiple times.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sinking land to '0' in-place avoids an external visited boolean matrix, running in O(M*N) time with O(M*N) worst-case frontier space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Four-directional boundary checks, sinking visited land cells in-place or using visited set, correct component counting.
